text:
anya: Quick pass on the fanout vs bulk (non-stream) SLO sweep I ran this morning. Put the charts here: https://redwood-internal.s3/bench/1719501234-fanout-bulk.png :chart_with_upwards_trend:

kevin: Nice, can you TL;DR numbers? p95/p50 and throughput for H100 vs A100?

anya: TL;DR — for the Llama-variant (32k context) with int8 kernels:
- H100 (us-west1): SSE streaming (single-client fanout) p50 ~ 18ms token, p95 ~ 75ms, sustainable throughput ~ 4.2k tok/s per GPU.
- H100 (us-west1): Non-stream HTTP+batched (bulk) p50 ~ 35ms token, p95 ~ 180ms, peak throughput ~ 11.5k tok/s per GPU (higher batch util).
- A100 (eu-west3): SSE p50 ~ 26ms, p95 ~ 120ms, throughput ~ 3.1k tok/s.
- A100 (eu-west3): Non-stream bulk p50 ~ 48ms, p95 ~ 240ms, throughput ~ 8.2k tok/s.

rachel: So streaming gives way better tail for interactive but lower aggregate throughput. Matches intuition. What about prefix caching impact?

anya: With prefix/KV cache warm (same prefix across fanout): streaming p95 drops ~20% on H100, throughput up ~15%. For bulk, cache helps latency slightly but doesn't move the throughput knee much (batching dominates).

kevin: What kernel/quant flags did you use? any fused-attn vs flash-attn differences?

anya: Bench configs in the bucket: https://redwood-internal.s3/bench/1719501234-configs.json. Short: int8-tdq with GEMM-fused kernels on H100 (cuBLAS+custom kernels), A100 used fallback kernels (slightly less efficient for kv copy). Flash-attn path only used on H100 for short sequences — for 32k we rely on block-attn fallback which costs more memcpy.

model-bench-bot: Automated note: baseline evals completed: 1200 requests, 95% CI for p95 within +-3ms for H100 runs. Attachments: s3://redwood-internal/bench/1719501234-raw.csv

rachel: Any numbers for websocket fanout (many small clients) vs SSE single stream?

anya: Websocket fanout (100 concurrent clients, small tokens per req):
- H100: median per-client latency ~ 22ms, p95 ~ 90ms, aggregate throughput ~ 3.8k tok/s (due to per-connection overhead).
- SSE fanout (keep-alive single stream multiplex): per-client median lower (~16ms) and aggregate ~4.0k tok/s. So SSE multiplexing helps a bit on the runtime path because we avoid full socket handshake + per-connection buffers.

kevin: Interesting. For rollout: if prod traffic is chatty (many short prompts) -> prefer streaming endpoints on H100. If batch/embeddings-heavy -> non-stream endpoints on A100 clusters to save $/tok. Agree?

devex: +1. We should add a canary config that routes 10% of traffic to streaming H100 pool and 90% to bulk A100 for the next week for customer X. Any caveats?

anya: Caveats: model variant parity (quantization noise) across kernels. I saw a tiny quality drift for int8-tdq on H100 vs A100 fp16 baseline — need an eval sweep on the prompt set used by the customer. Also watch for p95 spikes when multiple fanouts coincide (burst).

kevin: Can you paste the curl examples for both endpoints so infra can wire health checks?

anya: Sure:
```
# SSE streaming
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"llama-32k-q8","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
\n# Non-stream bulk
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"llama-32k-q8","input":"<batch of prompts>"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
model-bench-bot: CI note: regression check flagged 0.6% BLEU drift for int8 on one prompt shard (investigate).

rachel: Ok let's add quant eval to the canary gate and set an alert if p95 > 2x baseline for more than 5m.

anya: I'll upload a small playbook in the same bucket with rollout steps and the graphs. Link: https://redwood-internal.s3/bench/1719501234-rollout-playbook.md :eyes:

kevin: Thanks — this is actionable. I'll spin up canary infra and ping infra on the ticket.

devex: tagging @oncall for FYI during the canary. :thumbsup:
